bibliographic_source.title: Reducing Floating Point Error in Dot Product Using the Superblock Family of Algorithms

paper_locations.anchor: Relative-error model, gamma notation, explicit exclusion of overflow and underflow, and postload blocked special case
t-level equal-block superblock algorithm and bound gamma_(t*(N^(1/t)-1)+1)*|x|^T|y|
Three-level fixed-block implementation gives additional evidence for intended carry propagation

task_clarification: For every admissible positive integer level count t and vector length N with an integer equal blocking factor B satisfying B^t=N, compute the t-level superblock dot product: round each input product; sum B entries per lowest block and combine B child block totals per next level, recursively, in the source's natural order.

Under the source's standard relative-error model excluding both overflow and underflow, and the gamma-validity condition, formalize |computed dot product - exact x^T y| ≤ gamma_(t*(B-1)+1)*sum_i |x_i*y_i| for arbitrary signed inputs.

Include source endpoints t=1 (canonical dot product) and t=2 (postload blocked) as well as every integral t-level equal-block case. The library's existing two-level result is a component, not a substitute for the complete t-level theorem.
scope_constraints: The exact output must arise from the t-level algorithm, not from a preassumed error-bound interface. Retain rounding of every product and every level's additions.

Figure 3.1(a) prints 'for (j=t-2; j; j--)', which does skip level zero and makes the literal program wrong even at t=2. This task explicitly selects the mathematical equal-block hierarchy defined by the adjacent Section 3 prose, Figure 3.2, and Proposition 3.1, not the literal defective program. The source defect must be disclosed in every report; if independent review judges the intended algorithm still ambiguous, exclude this task.
Do not narrow to nonnegative inputs, a fixed t, or a non-source blocking factor. The paper explicitly assumes integral block-size calculations for clarity.
Preserve the exact error-counter coefficient t*(B-1)+1 and the absolute-input dot-product scale |x|^T|y|; a norm or one-level gamma_N bound is not the target.
The library already proves a related two-level Castaldo bound, so collision review must distinguish the full t-level theorem from that existing declaration.
